answer: The ocean multiplier is published, charged in yarrow, and hollow lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 827 identities would post 738 proofs and burn roughly 18 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
